correctness.rationale: The cyclic spectrum, orientation convention and fixed weight are consistent. More precisely than the opening sentence of Step 1, the complement of a window containing all three ones lies inside the interior of one gap; a shortest such window uses the complement of the interior of a largest gap and has length n−max(g)+1. A three-one factor fixes two ordered step gaps and hence the third. Without such a factor, a fixed two-one pattern at step distance d<k occurs once for each gap d; its outside marker cannot appear in the window. For every fixed one position, the preceding and following marker exclusions are disjoint; the all-zero count sums max(g−k,0). Thus the spectrum depends only on the gap multiset and records the multiplicities of all gaps <k. At K=floor(2n/3) the bound H=n−K is strictly below K and 3H−n≤2, forcing a repeat in each triple-free gap multiset. At k0=K−1 the deficits from H=n−k0 sum to 3, 5 or 4 by residue; partitioning these totals into three distinct nonnegative parts gives exactly the stated gap lists, with the listed positivity condition. The short-gap counts recover the multiset at k0 for n=6 or n≥8 because H≤k0 (unseen gaps, if any, equal k0). At n=7, if two gaps are unseen they both equal 3 by their sum bound; if one is unseen its value is determined by the total, and three unseen gaps are impossible. This excludes cross-multiset boundary collisions everywhere. Prefixing each factor proves monotonicity in k. The n=3,4 domains are singletons and the n=5 gap multisets {1,1,3} and {1,2,2} have different 11 counts at k=2. Independently enumerated literal cyclic factor counters for n=6..80 agreed with the threshold boundary and every listed doubleton and reversal pairing.
